sources.entry: Mumble - Low-latency, high quality voice/text chat software. (Source Code, Clients) BSD-3-Clause C++/deb

summary.one_liner: Mumble is an open-source, low-latency voice-chat program (client and server) written on Qt and Opus.
summary.what_it_does: Mumble is a voice-chat application with two modules: the client (mumble) and the server (mumble-server, formerly murmur). The README says the client runs on Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD and macOS, and the server should run on anything Qt can be installed on. The server is run from the command line with options for setting the SuperUser password, choosing an alternate ini file, running in the foreground, and verbose logging. The README also describes an OpenGL overlay that draws the Mumble GUI over games via LD_PRELOAD or the mumble-overlay command. Translations are handled through Weblate, and general-purpose plugins are supported. Build instructions are kept in separate documentation that varies by branch.
use_cases: group voice chat with friends or team
how_to_run: Install the Mumble client from your distribution packages or the Windows/macOS downloads
Run mumble-server --set-su-pw <password> to set the SuperUser password
Edit mumble-server.ini using the configuration template in the repository
Optionally run the official Docker image (instructions linked from the README)
notable: Separate client and server modules; server formerly named murmur
OpenGL overlay that draws the GUI over games via LD_PRELOAD
Server can run on any platform Qt supports
Multiple server instances from one directory using --ini
caveats: Build instructions depend on branch; master is unstable development code
macOS server is distributed separately as Static OS X Server
The SuperUser account is disabled until a password is set
